subjects.displayTitle: Friendship with all: kindness beyond the familiar circle
subjects.introduction: Never ask whether a person deserves to be loved. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sets that condition aside at the outset: kindness is to fall like rain and sunshine on every field, and the fruitful tree gives its fruit even to the one who throws stones at it. Bahá’u’lláh asks the same of speech. Whoever holds a jewel of truth may offer it in the kindliest language, and if it is refused must leave the other person to himself and pray for him, never treating him unkindly; a gentle tongue, He says, draws hearts as a lodestone draws iron. Friendship on these terms reaches the traveller from Turkey or Japan who should be made to feel at home, the follower of another religion whose scripture is to be read with reverence, and the disheartened soul who needs to be drawn back into the circle. It has its wisdom too, for goodwill toward everyone is not closeness to harmful conduct. The Buddhist discourse on loving-kindness, which wishes well to beings near and far, keeps company with these teachings. From here the road leads toward loving one’s enemies, the golden rule and regard for one’s neighbour, and a life spent in service to humanity.
subjects.arc: Begin with unconditional kindness, respect and freedom of response; widen friendship across religious and social divisions; consider discernment and return to practical, sustained service.

order.why: Offer conviction with goodwill and freedom to decline.
Open by removing the test of deservingness from kindness.
shortened: Wherefore must the loved ones of God associate in affectionate fellowship with stranger and friend alike, showing forth to all the utmost loving-kindness, disregarding the degree of their capacity, never asking whether they deserve to be loved. In every instance let the friends be considerate and infinitely kind.

order.why: Give strangers an explicit claim to respect.
Set respect for rights beside freedom from contention.
shortened: Say: Contend not with anyone, nor deny any soul's rights.

order.why: Make welcome concrete in conversation and assistance.
Imagine impartial care through sun, rain and spring breeze.
Read the fruitful tree giving even to those who throw stones.
Unite universality with justice, protection and truthfulness.
shortened: Therefore, with divine strength, heavenly resolve, merciful intention, and spiritual qualities, associate with all people in every land with love, kindness and righteous conduct. For in this glorious Dispensation, the divine bounty is all-encompassing and triumph complete. All conduct and behavior must be universal, not particular - there are no exceptions. Man is commanded to show justice, fairness, trustworthiness, nobility, love, truthfulness, fellowship, consideration, protection and kindness towards all the peoples of the world.

order.why: Connect the well-being of everyone with true peace.
shortened: True peace and tranquillity will only be realized when every soul will have become the well-wisher of all mankind.

order.why: Include shelter, companionship and support for the alone.
shortened: Be a refuge and shelter for strangers, and grant those who are alone assistance and support. Be a remedy for every pain and a balm for every wound. Become intimate with all peoples of the world and a respected companion to all nations.

order.why: Notice the person who has become disheartened.
shortened: If someone becomes disheartened, give them importance and by whatever means warm their hearts and bring them into your circle.

order.why: Give kindness practical forms across generations.
Develop those familial roles without dwelling on shortcomings.
shortened: In any case, the divine friends in those regions and frontiers must associate with all souls with utmost radiance, love and kindness, and must not look to the shortcomings, laxity and veils of souls. They must be loving to all humanity, become sons to elderly people, take on the role of father to youths, and become kind brothers to peers and equals.

order.why: Read the reported commitment not to send people away unaided.
shortened: We do not look at the evil deeds of the people. We do not consider the race, the religion or nationality. We do our utmost to help everyone.
The inhabitants of these parts know this and therefore whenever they are in difficulties or have had business reverses they come to us and we will never send them away unaided or deprived.

order.why: Keep the recorded appeal for assistance without racial or religious distinction.
Attend to the reported special concern for poor people.
Read the call to raise the fallen and cheer the hopeless.
Imagine care through water, food, healing and restored dignity.
shortened: O thou maid-servant of God! The utmost desire of the lordly ones is the union of the friends, the agreement of the believers and the spiritual communication of the hearts; in order that they may shine in this darkened world like unto bright stars; educate all the communities of the world in the precepts of love; be kind and benevolent to every one, sympathetic and compassionate to all; to become the cool and pure water to every thirsty one, a heavenly table to every hungry one, a swift healing antidote to every sick one and the cause of the everlasting glory to every humiliated one.

order.why: Pair gentleness with active help.
shortened: Be kind and gentle with all the people of the world and serve and assist everyone with the utmost love.

order.why: Bring the circle of kindness to neighboring farms.
Locate universal duty in the particular community of Beirut.
Include a concrete request to welcome a visitor.
shortened: Therefore, in all cities the friends of God should welcome him and show the utmost respect and consideration, so that it may be observed how kind and appreciative the friends of God are.

order.why: Begin from relatives and extend the same conduct to outsiders.
Condense equal kindness to friend and stranger.
Replace the idea of strangers with kinship and honored friendship.
Question the division between insiders and outsiders.
shortened: Therefore the friends must consider strangers as friends and regard those outside as inside. They must consider the deprived ones as confidants, bestow melody upon the melody-less, regard the wayward as people of guidance, make no distinction between them.

order.why: Describe kindness that makes a stranger familiar.
shortened: The divine friends must employ all means to become friendly with strangers, that is, show the utmost kindness so that the stranger becomes familiar and the deprived one becomes privy to secrets.

order.why: Make service a setting for new bonds of fellowship.
shortened: Among other things, he can engage in service, establish bonds of fellowship with everyone, and with the utmost spirituality make strangers into friends.

order.why: Resist treating an unpolished mirror as an enemy.
Answer need with education and care rather than disdain.
shortened: We must associate with all humanity in gentleness and kindliness. We must love all with love of the heart. Some are ignorant; they must be trained and educated. One is sick; he must be healed. Another is as a child; we must assist him to attain maturity. We must not detest him who is ailing, neither shun him, scorn nor curse him, but care for him with the utmost kindness and tenderness. An infant must not be treated with disdain simply because it is an infant. Our responsibility is to train, educate and develop it in order that it may advance toward maturity.

order.why: Regard people as God’s creation beyond judgments about their condition.
shortened: Therefore, one must purify one's vision and not regard the limitations and conditions of creation. Whether obedient or disobedient, one must consider all people as God's servants, and whether human or inhuman, must regard all as God's creation and must treat all accordingly. O friends of God! Serve humanity with utmost joy and radiance, and show forth love to all mankind.

order.why: Apply truthfulness equally to friend and enemy.
Name the qualities needed for trustworthy relationships.
shortened: Deal with all peoples of the earth with the utmost kindness, sincerity, trustworthiness, nobility, goodwill and care. Counter evil with good and respond to faithlessness with faithfulness.

order.why: Read the brief universal counsel on good character.
Extend fidelity and fellowship across religious groupings.
shortened: One must deal with all human beings of whatever religion or group with the utmost friendship, truthfulness, trustworthiness, godliness, fellowship and unity.
Rather, we must sacrifice ourselves for strangers, let alone friends; we must worship others, let alone loved ones.

order.why: Enter the sustained call for universal love and a generous response to hostility.
shortened: It is incumbent upon everyone to show the utmost love, rectitude of conduct, straightforwardness and sincere kindliness unto all the peoples and kindreds of the world, be they friends or strangers. So intense must be the spirit of love and loving kindness, that the stranger may find himself a friend, the enemy a true brother, no difference whatsoever existing between them. For universality is of God and all limitations earthly.

Should other peoples and nations be unfaithful to you show your fidelity unto them, should they be unjust toward you show justice towards them, should they keep aloof from you attract them to yourselves, should they show their enmity be friendly towards them, should they poison your lives, sweeten their souls, should they inflict a wound upon you, be a salve to their sores.

order.why: Read the text’s account of the scope of love in this age.
Hear the call to transform enmity through sacrificial kindness.
Hear love without preference described as foundational.
shortened: In this divine cycle and merciful manifestation, the very foundation of God's Faith is love and kindliness, though not bound by any limitations. One must show love and compassion to all the peoples of the world with utmost joy, gladness and delight. No distinction or preference should be made.

order.why: Connect one human body with fellowship across religions.
shortened: Beware lest the desires of the flesh and of a corrupt inclination provoke divisions among you. Be ye as the fingers of one hand, the members of one body. Thus counselleth you the Pen of Revelation, if ye be of them that believe.
Consort ye then with the followers of all religions, and proclaim ye the Cause of your Lord, the Most Compassionate; this is the very crown of deeds, if ye be of them who understand.
Consort with all religions with amity and concord, that they may inhale from you the sweet fragrance of God.

order.why: Receive joyful association as a glad tiding.
Consider its relationship to fairness, order and social renewal.
Keep the Tablet of the World’s concise restatement.
Retain the separate statement of the new commandment.
Read the direct reference to the Most Holy Book.
Keep the same counsel in its distinct source address.
Preserve the explanatory appeal to the explicit text.
Understand fellowship as freedom from animosity and ideas of uncleanness.
shortened: Regarding association with followers of other religions about which you inquired, according to the explicit text of the Kitab-i-Aqdas it is "Associate with all religions with joy and fragrance." The intention of this verse is that the people of Baha should have no ill will or animosity toward any group, but should act with love toward all, not considering others unclean or avoiding them.

order.why: Link it with freedom from prejudice.
Read the invitation to embrace people of all religions.
Keep kindness as the measure of that association.
shortened: Deal with all peoples and religions with utmost kindness.

order.why: Hear the reported call to read and honor others’ scriptures.
shortened: We must affiliate with all the religions and sects; speak to them from their own standpoint and show to them in practice that we love their books, we read their scriptures, and we honor and respect the founders of their religions.

order.why: Consider the reported invitation to enter one another’s places of worship.
shortened: Everyone must do away with false prejudices and must even go to the other churches and mosques, for, in all of these worshiping places, the name of God is mentioned. Since all gather to worship God, what difference does it make? None of these worship satan. The Mohammedans must go to the churches of the Christians and of the Jews and vice-versa, the others must go to the Mohammedan mosques.

order.why: Read the address’s proposal for acknowledging another tradition’s sacred figures.
Keep the reported connection between reverent speech and reconciliation.
Make sincere interaction and respectful remembrance explicit.
Retain the reported instruction to avoid debasing religious statements.
Read the rejection of cursing and denouncing others.
shortened: Do not pronounce as infidels those who have recognized God, and curse not those who recite the verses of God with humility.

order.why: Reject turning scripture into a cause of hatred.
shortened: Associate, O My loved ones, with the followers of all religions in a spirit of friendliness and fellowship. Beware lest ye make God's Word an occasion for your disputation or a cause for manifesting hatred among you.

order.why: Condemn rancor while encouraging association with different groups.
Preserve the parallel prohibition in its own source.
shortened: Associate with the followers of all religions, O My loved ones, in a spirit of friendliness and fellowship. Beware lest ye make the Word of God the cause of your differences or a pretext for manifesting hatred among you.

order.why: Notice the gracious response to doubt about one’s own faith.
shortened: We are in perfect joy and fragrance with all religions, in complete fellowship with all, neither harshness. We think of love and mercy for all, not difficulty. We are commanded to friendship and intimacy, not hatred and estrangement.
If they doubt our faith, we fully acknowledge their mystical insight.

order.why: Keep the reported marriage example and its historical setting.
shortened: The marriage of the Baha'is was also performed according to Christian rites, so that the world may know that the people of Baha are not confined by trivial customs, that they respect all nations and their peoples, that they are free from all prejudices and associate with all religions with utmost peace and happiness.

order.why: Retain the recorded inclusive image of a tree and its branches.
shortened: Every community finds the reality of its principles in this Cause. The Baha'i Cause is like a tree and these various communities, or gatherings or societies, are branches. When you compare the tree with the branches you find every branch in the tree, and this is the Baha'i Cause.

order.why: Read the reported counsel to preserve existing bonds.
Keep the reported answer on the universal scope of a divine birth.
Consider removal of bias as a path toward unity.
shortened: This bias will be removed and when it is removed, people will live in friendliness, kindness and love which will bring forth unity.

order.why: Read the account of love beyond exclusive bonds.
shortened: The great unselfish love for humanity is bounded by none of these imperfect, semi-selfish bonds; this is the one perfect love, possible to all mankind, and can only be achieved by the power of the Divine Spirit. No worldly power can accomplish the universal love.

order.why: Keep the reported distinction between love and possession.
shortened: If you love your country, love it not with the narrow feeling that it must be loved because it is yours alone, but with the greater consciousness that your home is a part of the universe. If you love brother or comrade or wife, love each one as a part of God, and not with the narrow sense of possession which renders the love selfish and exclusive.

order.why: Distinguish universal love from personal attraction in the recorded account.
shortened: We must love all humanity as the children of God. Even if they kill us, we must die with love for them. It is not possible for us to love everybody with a personal love, but we must love all humanity alike.

order.why: Explore the difficulty of loving someone who lacks familiar attractions.
shortened: It is easy for us to love a friend or even an animal, but how difficult to love one who is without attraction. Yet if the Love of God is shining in our hearts, we, like Christ, may see that Love reflected in every personality, and love all alike.

order.why: Read sympathy as attention to another’s higher aims.
Keep the reported invitation to expect good of others.
shortened: He said we must consider all people--not only believers--to be good. He hoped every one would be good.

order.why: Add humility to the practice of fraternity.
shortened: We are all the children of one Father; the sheep of one Shepard; the members of one family; the birds of one orchard, the flowers of one rose-garden, the waves of one sea, the rays of one Sun; the stars of one heaven and the servants of One God.
Let us all be humble before the signs of God and treat each other as brothers.

order.why: Return to the broad relationship among unity, protection and kindly speech.
shortened: The utterance of God is a lamp, whose light is these words: Ye are the fruits of one tree, and the leaves of one branch. Deal ye one with another with the utmost love and harmony, with friendliness and fellowship. He Who is the Daystar of Truth beareth Me witness! So powerful is the light of unity that it can illuminate the whole earth.
Exert yourselves that ye may attain this transcendent and most sublime station, the station that can insure the protection and security of all mankind.

order.why: Protect freedom from objection while inviting an offering of what one knows.
Retain the reported demand that kindness survive refusal.
shortened: It is of course a great sin to reject these Teachings, and it is our duty to persuade and teach people to embrace this Truth; But if they should reject it, we must bear it with patience, and we are to remain toward them exactly what we were before. If, however you find a person leading a truly good earnest life, who does not wish to hear or receive these Teachings, you are to remember what our Lord Jesus said, "He that is not against me is with Me."

order.why: Read intimate association as a setting for sharing a teaching.
shortened: When Abdul-Baha inquired the condition and the association of the friends, it was intimated that unlike the days gone by the friends are intimately associating with all the people of every shade and opinion, of every sect, and social standing. He said: "Such is the way that must be adopted, for only through intimate association will the friends be able to teach and sow a seed in the heart of a seeker. The flower must be brought close and near in order to inhale its scent and fragrance."

order.why: Keep the recorded challenge to widen one’s circle.
Introduce bonds of fellowship as part of teaching.
Place joy and kindness within that encounter.
shortened: When any of the friends associate with the heedless ones, they should, with utmost kindness and joy, become the cause of their awareness and the means of their remembrance.

order.why: Join guidance to wisdom and merciful conduct.
Share wisdom in a spirit of joy.
shortened: Consort with all peoples with joy and fragrance, then remind them of that which ye possess of wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Relate association to remembrance of a religious claim.
shortened: Say: Consort with all religions with joy and fragrance, and remind them of that which hath appeared in creation. Should they turn towards it, it is for their own good; and should they turn away, withdraw from them and remain steadfast in great dignity.

order.why: Read the invitation through the image of fragrance.
Preserve the source’s unfinished excerpt without supplying its missing conclusion.
Connect kindly fellowship with proclamation.
shortened: Blessed is he who associateth with all peoples in a spirit of utmost kindliness and good-fellowship, and telleth them of this announcement with which every mighty book and every perspicuous tablet hath been adorned.

order.why: Consider character and an illumined heart as conditions of sharing.
shortened: All must associate with the peoples of the world with radiant faces and illumined hearts, that perchance they may hearken from the people of Truth, glorified be His majesty, that which conduceth to maturity, attainment, and guidance.

order.why: Read affection as an invitation to awakening.
shortened: Deal with the servants with utmost love, fellowship, affection and unity, that perchance the sleeping ones may awaken and turn towards the Friend.

order.why: Treat good character itself as a guide.
shortened: Associate with all the peoples of the world with the utmost spirit, fragrance, dignity and composure, that your goodly character may spread its fragrance among them. This fragrance hath ever been and shall ever remain a guide.

order.why: Consider conduct that attracts hearts and friendship that encourages devotion.
Include humility toward those one recognizes as spiritually fragrant.
shortened: Should thou find those from whose hearts waft the sweet savors of the Beloved, associate with them and show humility toward them.

order.why: Retain the reported ideal of learning from and contributing to an encounter.
shortened: Man must always associate with those from whom he can get light, or be with those to whom he can give light. He must either receive or give instructions. Otherwise, being with people without these two intentions, he is spending his time for nothing, and, by so doing, he is neither gaining nor causing others to gain.

order.why: Keep the recorded preference for sincere seekers in its particular setting.
Contrast courteous approach with estrangement through avoidance.
shortened: Wisdom requires that they deal with the divines and the descendants of the Prophet with love, as love may guide some to the straight path. Avoidance and distance have been and are the cause of estrangement. In the Most Holy Book He says, blessed and exalted be His utterance: "Consort with the followers of all religions with joy and fragrance. Thus hath the light of Our guidance shone forth from the horizon of wisdom and utterance. Hold ye fast unto it. This is the command which the All-Wise, the Faithful, hath revealed from His Most Great Prison."

order.why: Include forbearance and consideration toward clergy.
shortened: Let them show some forbearance, exercise consideration, not tear away the veil, and deal with the clergy and others with the utmost kindness, consideration and regard.

order.why: Read association with officials in relation to relief for the oppressed.
shortened: This was presented before His presence, and He said: "This matter is most praiseworthy. In the Kitab-i-Aqdas, all are permitted to associate with different groups, and association with rulers and officials is permissible for several beneficial purposes. Through such association, oftentimes an oppressed one may find deliverance, or a prisoner may be freed, and perchance words may be spoken that cause awakening. Association with such persons is a hundred thousand times preferable to association with the heedless divines and theologians.

order.why: Preserve the particular reference to the Chief Secretary.
Recognize compassion maintained across communities during war.
shortened: Praise be to God that the friends of Baku were, throughout these years of war, at peace with all communities, and, in conformity with the Divine teachings, compassionate unto all.

order.why: Connect truthful public service with love among people.
Calls for loving association with all peoples without distinction.
Retain the counsel about political non-interference within its source setting.
shortened: Fifth is preventing all from that which causes sedition and corruption, complete non-interference in political affairs, refraining from conversation in this regard even to the slightest degree, and indicating submission in all conditions and tranquility and love and friendship with all.

order.why: Introduce wisdom as a continuing qualification of association.
shortened: In all circumstances be mindful of wisdom and associate with all in a spirit of fragrance and joy.

order.why: Link that wisdom with intention and attention to divine counsel.
Read the reported distinction between religious difference and antagonistic conduct.
Keep the reported warning that shared religious identity does not excuse harmful character.
Consider the recorded distinction between kindness and welcoming a threat.
Preserve the reported counsel for distance without harshness or gossip.
Keep the particular reported limit concerning harm to the Cause.
Place the explicit rejection of bloodshed and corruption beside these questions of conduct.
shortened: Say: O people! Fear God, shed not blood, oppose no soul, and be of the doers of good. Beware lest ye spread corruption in the land after its reformation, and follow not the ways of the heedless.

order.why: Read removal of killing as part of the context for religious fellowship.
Hear the demand for patience and humanity even toward enemies.
shortened: With the utmost patience, tranquility, trustworthiness, religiosity, love, kindness and humanity, interact and deal with all people of all communities and nations. Know nothing but goodwill, good conduct and care, even toward bloodthirsty enemies.

order.why: Preserve the challenging account of goodwill toward an oppressor.
shortened: They look upon all humanity with utmost love, even if they fall into danger. They show faithfulness to the oppressor; if they are harmed, they seek comfort and blessing for the tyrant.

order.why: Read consideration toward enemies amid grief and trials.
Turn ill-wishing into an occasion for well-wishing.
shortened: Therefore you must seek fellowship with all people and pursue friendship with all nations. Do not object to anyone, do not cause anyone to be hurt. Win hearts and free souls from snares and traps. Rather, be well-wishers to ill-wishers and become heart and soul friends to enemies. Consider strangers as familiar and others as friends.

order.why: Condense the same universal invitation.
Include loving care toward a stubborn denier.
Read patient kindness in a village where objections persist.
shortened: In any case, show the utmost kindness to the people in that village. Pay no heed to their turning away, objections, exaggeration and pride. Show kindness to all for the sake of God. Assuredly this will have an effect and thou wilt find companions.

order.why: Keep the resolve to be a trusted friend without exception.
shortened: Bend thou with tenderness over the servitors of the All-Merciful, that thou mayest hoist the sail of love upon the ark of peace that moveth across the seas of life. Let nothing grieve thee, and be thou angered at none. It behooveth thee to be content with the Will of God, and a true and loving and trusted friend to all the peoples of the earth, without any exceptions whatever. This is the quality of the sincere, the way of the saints, the emblem of those who believe in the unity of God, and the raiment of the people of Baha.

order.why: Connect the absence of imagined strangers with wishing for peace.
shortened: As long as thou canst, wish thou the most great peace for mankind: Associate with all in perfect love and kindness; hold all dear and count all friends and familiar ones; know no enemies; imagine no strangers.

order.why: Consider overlooking faults as part of communal concord.
shortened: If any differences arise amongst you, behold Me standing before your face, and overlook the faults of one another for My name's sake and as a token of your love for My manifest and resplendent Cause. We love to see you at all times consorting in amity and concord within the paradise of My good-pleasure, and to inhale from your acts the fragrance of friendliness and unity, of loving-kindness and fellowship. Thus counseleth you the All-Knowing, the Faithful. We shall always be with you; if We inhale the perfume of your fellowship, Our heart will assuredly rejoice, for naught else can satisfy Us.

order.why: Recognize the injury caused by internal discord.
Read the reported relation between love among believers and wider friendship.
Extend mutual kindness outward to others.
shortened: They must show the utmost kindness to one another, and likewise show perfect mercy and generosity to others, associate with all in utmost love, and occupy themselves with the mention of God.

order.why: Keep the recorded link between association and mutual assistance.
shortened: Therefore this free-will in man which God has created in man's being is the cause of adornment. Consequently be ye kind toward each other, associate with one another, assist and help one another.

order.why: Pray for cooperation among strangers and kin.
Connect spiritual companionship across distance with aid for the helpless.
Widen education and goodwill toward the well-being of humankind.
shortened: He Who is the Eternal Truth hath, from the Day Spring of Glory, directed His eyes towards the people of Baha, and is addressing them in these words: Address yourselves to the promotion of the well-being and tranquillity of the children of men. Bend your minds and wills to the education of the peoples and kindreds of the earth, that haply the dissensions that divide it may, through the power of the Most Great Name, be blotted out from its face, and all mankind become the upholders of one Order, and the inhabitants of one City.
Blessed is he who mingleth with all men in a spirit of utmost kindliness and love.

order.why: Make mingling with others an expression of human oneness.
shortened: Mingle with all people and unfurl the banner of the oneness in the world of humanity.

order.why: Read the reported moral distinction between fellowship and warfare.
Pray for a life that reduces war and spreads tranquility.
Consider reconciliation as a requirement of worship.
Gather the ethical qualities into becoming a healing balm.
Focus aspiration on conduct and its effects.
shortened: Now you Persian friends must concentrate your thoughts on divine conduct and kindness toward humanity and godly behavior, so that it may produce great effects in this world.

order.why: Restrain reproach while cultivating trustworthy fellowship.
Join detachment with kindness toward people.
Keep the reported image of detachment expressed through association.
shortened: If with this state of severance they associated with mankind, teaching them the precepts of sanctity and purity, each one of them would have shone forth like unto a sun.

order.why: Relate worldly encounter to a spiritual horizon.
shortened: Associate with all people, keeping your gaze fixed upon the horizon of grace.

order.why: Read friendship alongside freedom from attachment.
Consider love for the world for the sake of the Beloved.
Use the image of love’s light to gather the theme.
shortened: They must associate with all people with the spirit of fellowship and with love and affection. Love is God's light among His creation; through it every light appears and the world is illumined by it.

order.why: Refresh the downcast through friendship and charity.
shortened: This is the Day whereon the Ocean of God’s mercy hath been manifested unto men, the Day in which the Daystar of His loving-kindness hath shed its radiance upon them, the Day in which the clouds of His bountiful favor have overshadowed the whole of mankind. Now is the time to cheer and refresh the downcast through the invigorating breeze of love and fellowship, and the living waters of friendliness and charity.

order.why: Move beyond self toward the neighbor with joy.
Make joyful association an expression of gratitude.
Join thanksgiving with gentle dealings.
Read fellowship with friend and stranger as a source of gladness.
shortened: In any case, be confident in the novel favors of the Wondrous One and always engage in joy and delight and happiness and gladness and fellowship and love with friend and stranger alike.

order.why: Seek to become a joy to others.
shortened: Become loving friends to all humanity and a joy to the hearts and souls of all the world.

order.why: Encourage those who will carry kindness onward.
shortened: Inspire and encourage the divine friends with the fragrances of the All-Merciful, spiritual attractions and merciful sentiments, so that all may associate and conduct themselves with utmost kindness toward all people.

order.why: Include the aspiration to kindness toward every nation.
shortened: Show such kindness to all people of all nations that praise and acclamation may reach the ears of the soul from the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Read tenderness as an active form of friendship.
shortened: The friends of God must associate with the spirit of friendship with other souls and show to them infinite love and tenderness.

order.why: Consider kindness as a life-giving presence.
shortened: Be kind to all souls, breathe the breath of life and attract hearts to the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Make mercy toward humanity a shared vocation.
shortened: The loved ones of God must be a mercy to all mankind and loving towards all humanity. They must associate with everyone in a spirit of joy and fragrance.

order.why: Hear the invitation to a season of friendship.
shortened: This is the time for gladness and the season for friendship and kindness toward all peoples and nations. Behave with heavenly attributes so that you may become manifestations of divine mercy.

order.why: Pray for knowledge expressed in benevolence toward religious communities.
shortened: Verily I beseech God to assist thee with the spirit of knowledge and enable thee to be good and benevolent to all the people of religions.

order.why: Pray to become a sign of mercy for all creation.
Join well-wishing with truthfulness and steadiness.
shortened: Be loving towards all creation and wish well for all humanity. Be at peace with everyone and deal truthfully with all, that the eternal bounties of the All-Merciful may become thy companion and the effulgences of the All-Merciful may cause thee to become firm and steadfast in heart and step.

order.why: Read the blessing of a life of reconciliation.
Extend affectionate presence into every gathering.
Preserve the personal assurance of remembrance despite obstacles.
Retain the named expression of fidelity.
Become a loyal counselor and companion.
Keep the short universal command to love.
shortened: O friends! Be as lamps unto the darkened world and as light unto its gloom. Consort with all the peoples of the world with utmost love. All conflict, contention and corruption are forbidden in this Most Great Revelation.

order.why: Retain the recorded acknowledgment of commanded association.
shortened: People who call on me almost every day carry on a stream of profitless, unspiritual talk and I must listen to them with patience. We are commanded to associate with all the people.

order.why: Let the brief recorded imperative address the reader directly.
shortened: Question: "What is the Baha'i Faith?"
Answer: "Trust in God. Be kind to thy fellowmen.

order.why: Hear the reported call to become a dawning-place of love.
shortened: We should associate with all peoples and religions of the world with perfect love and oneness, for the Blessed Beauty says: "O people of Baha! You have been and are the dawning-places of love and the daysprings of divine grace and bounty.

order.why: Read the counsel of the Wronged One to associate joyfully.
Bring the invitation to each encounter.

order.why: Return to the plain command of utmost love.
shortened: Say: O friends! This is the day of goodly character and righteous deeds. Associate with all the peoples of the world with the utmost love.

order.why: Reflect on a heart that harbors no intention to harm.
End the source-linked sequence with love for everyone carried into sleep.
Open the supplied readings by stepping beyond racial mistrust.

shortened: It is not merely material well-being that people need. What they desperately need is to know how to live their lives -- they need to know who they are, to what purpose they exist, and how they should act towards one another; and, once they know the answers to these questions they need to be helped to gradually apply these answers to every-day behaviour.

Their whole energy is directed towards the building of the good, a good which has such a positive strength that in the face of it the multitude of evils -- which are in essence negative -- will fade away and be no more. To enter into the quixotic tournament of demolishing one by one the evils in the world is, to a Baha'i, a vain waste of time and effort.

subjects.displayTitle: Music and singing: a ladder for the soul, a language of fellowship
subjects.introduction: Sound is only vibration in the air, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes, and yet see how it moves the heart. Bahá’u’lláh goes further: music is a ladder for the soul, made so that it may be lifted to the realm on high, with one warning: not to turn it into wings for self and passion. Where music had been thought reprehensible, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls it spiritual food and asks that children be taught to sing with excellence. A melody is a clear chalice; what fills it, and the state of the one who drinks, decide whether it gives life. He remembers a mystic guitarist weeping through a night of His childhood illness, and a boy with a flute by the Euphrates, as proof of a song’s power. The psalmist’s call for harp and trumpet, with sea and hills joining in, widens the chorus to all creation [1]. From here the path leads into gatherings where friends sing together, into the House of Worship whose hymns are meant to enrapture the Concourse on High, and into how the arts carry feeling between the material world and the spiritual.
subjects.arc: Begin with music’s wonder and its purpose; explore education, artistic excellence, intention and communal worship; follow musical imagery into joy, service and harmony.

order.why: Introduce music as a ladder and a responsibility.
shortened: We, verily, have made music as a ladder for your souls, a means whereby they may be lifted up unto the realm on high; make it not, therefore, as wings to self and passion.
They who recite the verses of the All-Merciful in the most melodious of tones will perceive in them that with which the sovereignty of earth and heaven can never be compared.

order.why: Open with the wonder of physical vibrations moving the heart.
Welcome music as nourishment and relief from sorrow.
shortened: Among certain nations of the East, music was considered reprehensible, but in this new age the Manifest Light hath, in His holy Tablets, specifically proclaimed that music, sung or played, is spiritual food for soul and heart.

The musician's art is among those arts worthy of the highest praise, and it moveth the hearts of all who grieve. Wherefore, O thou Shahnaz, play and sing out the holy words of God with wondrous tones in the gatherings of the friends, that the listener may be freed from chains of care and sorrow, and his soul may leap for joy and humble itself in prayer to the realm of Glory.

order.why: Place children’s talents and musical education near the beginning.
shortened: The art of music is divine and effective. It is the food of the soul and spirit. Through the power and charm of music the spirit of man is uplifted. It has wonderful sway and effect in the hearts of children, for their hearts are pure, and melodies have great influence in them. The latent talents with which the hearts of these children are endowed will find expression through the medium of music. Therefore, you must exert yourselves to make them proficient; teach them to sing with excellence and effect.

order.why: Challenge the musician to pursue excellence and finish the work.
Bring beautiful meaning, expression and melody into relationship.
shortened: Continue as long as thou canst this melody in the gatherings of the beloved; thus may the minds find rest and joy and become in tune with the love of God. When eloquence of expression, beauty of sense and sweetness of composition unite with new melodies the effect is ever great, especially if it be the anthem of the verses of oneness and the songs of praise to the Lord of Glory.

order.why: Ask what existing feelings music may awaken or intensify.
shortened: In the world of existence physical things have a connection with spiritual realities.

In short: melodies, though they are material, are connected with the spiritual, therefore, they produce a great effect. A certain kind of melody makes the spirit happy, another kind makes it sad, another excites it to action.
Whatever is in the heart of man, melody moves and awakens.
For instance: the music used in war awakens the desire for bloodshed. The meaning is that melody causes whatever feeling is in the heart to increase.

order.why: Make the listener’s inward orientation part of that question.
shortened: For example, a melody, sweet to the ear, bringeth the very spirit of life to a heart in love with God, yet staineth with lust a soul engrossed in sensual desires.

order.why: Allow spiritual effect across languages and musical modes.
shortened: The melody must be divine, whether it be in Persian, Arabic, or Turkish; the tune and air must be soul-stirring, whether in the mode of Hijaz or Iraq.

order.why: Keep the reported invitation to grow accustomed to unfamiliar music.
Explore the vessel-and-water image for music and sacred utterance.
shortened: Music is like this glass which is perfectly pure and polished. It is precisely like this clear chalice before us. And the Teachings and Utterances of God are like the water. When the chalice is in the utmost state of purity, absolutely clear and polished, and the water is perfectly fresh, then it will confer life. Wherefore, the Teachings of God, whether they be Utterances in the form of homilies, or prayers and communes, when they are melodiously chanted will proved most impressive.

order.why: Consider the union of earthly tunes and spiritual aspiration.
Read praise of musical science and the aspiration to harmony.
Make mastery an expression of service.
Include the encouragement to complete musical study.
Consider intention as a source of purpose in artistic learning.
shortened: For instance, when the studying of art is with the intention of obeying the command (of God) this study will certainly be done easily and great progress will soon be made therein; and when others discover this fragrance of spirituality in the action itself, this same will cause their awakening.

order.why: Pray for children to gain proficiency.
Read the recorded account of musical education and the remembered childhood musician.
shortened: The parents must see to it that their children are taught the best, classical music, such masterpieces that refine the souls and etherealize the aspirations. The life of a person who has learned to appreciate the artistic value and moral significance of music is redolent with brightness, health and joy.

Once during my early childhood I became very sick. At the time, my family lived in Teheran. I was lying in bed in a semi-conscious state. After much consultation the Doctors agreed upon a course of "musical treatment." Before sunset they brought into my room an old man with a very long beard. He carried under his 'Aba' a guitar. He sat near my bed and immediately began to play and sing. All through the night he played and sang, now in high, resonant voice and again in sweet, soft strains. My soul was charmed with his music. During certain hours of the night I opened my eyes and to my surprise I saw him weeping.

In the morning I felt better and asked my mother why the musician was weeping? She said: 'He was not a professional artist but a mystic worshipper of the Beloved. His singing was not mechanical, but an outpouring of the joy felt in his heart. His poems were mystic and allegorical addresses to the Adored One. Through his music he spoke to the hearts and quickened and moved them by the power of spirit. He did not make himself a slave of technique or enunciation but he sang the living truth, the eternal reality, hidden in the chambers of human consciousness. In his mysterious way, with the key of life, he opened the secret doors of beatitude and unlocked the gates of the higher and loftier vision.' Soon I became well and strong but the song and music of the mystic artist has ever been with me.

order.why: Keep the reported counsel to teach music that ennobles thought.
Include the reported encouragement to cultivate a beautiful voice.
Pursue versatility in melody and harmony.
Notice the care given to revising a poem for future work.
Invite composition with eloquence and depth.

Read the call to create a new ode for gatherings.
Encourage new meanings and pleasing melody together.
Hear the appreciation of significant and eloquent new verses.
shortened: How significant and eloquent were those new verses, for they were the notes of the clarion of the love of God!

order.why: Recognize a newly received song and its instruments.
Read the appreciation of Shahnaz’s composition.
shortened: O thou sweet-voiced Shahnaz,

The melody, which thou didst compose for the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar has reached the ears of 'Abdu'l-Baha. It was a very sweet and heart-touching melody, because it contained the praise and glorification of His Holiness Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Follow a received song into collective performance.
shortened: O thou who art rejoicing with the glad tidings of God!

Verily the Song of the Covenant of most eloquent phrase and of most wonderful melody was received. And the maidservants of the Merciful are singing it in the great assemblages and are rejoicing in these harmonies.

order.why: Consider a hymn traveling through translation.
shortened: Verily I shall send thy beautiful and new hymn to Persia so that they may translate and sing it in the assemblies.

order.why: Retain the expressed hope for a poem’s lasting life.
shortened: All poems shall be forgotten in the course of time save those that are extraordinary; thy poem shall be chanted with melody and best voices in the Center of Worship (or Mashrak-el-Azcar) forevermore.

order.why: Read the instructions for a particular festival song and its envisioned future.
shortened: With a melodious voice it should be sung during the Days of the Ridvan and the believers and maidservants of the Merciful must listen.

The poetries which are composed in these days will be mentioned by the poets and thinkers throughout the ages and after a thousand years they will be chanted and sung in the great meetings, vast congregations and wonderful Temples throughout the world.

order.why: Keep the reported historical account of Persian music attributed.
Hear the recorded discovery and encouragement of a young flutist.
shortened: At one time I was walking along the shore of Euphrates[.] Absorbed in my thought I suddenly heard the most charming and sweetest sound. I turned my head and saw a simple Arab lad riding on a donkey, loaded with under-brushes and playing on his flute. I was so intoxicated with the melody of his faultless tone that I requested him to get down from his donkey and play for me. I helped him to unload his donkey and then quietly we sat under the inviting shade of a tree. Then he began to play with such depth of feeling and beauty that my whole heart went to him. I drank deeply the sweet cadences and harmonies of his flute to such an extent that I was entranced thereby.

When he finished playing I assisted him again to load his donkey, gave him a present and the address of our house and asked him to call on me next day. At the appointed hour he came and played for us and as there were several prominent men in the room they all liked his music and asked him in turn to go to their homes one night a week and entertain them and their guests. In a short while he became famous throughout all Bagdad and leaving his hard labor of thorn-picking he devoted his career to the inspiring art of music. With his growing popularity he grew in wealth and position and became a respected, loved and honored member of the community. He was still in Bagdad when we were exiled to Constantinople and used to call on me almost every week antecedent to our departure.

order.why: Preserve the reported musical encounter and its spiritual analogy.
shortened: Last night an Hindu professor of music came here, bringing his musical instrument called The Vina with him and played for us certain oriental strains, accompanying them with singing - overhead our neighbor was playing the piano, but as soon as the professor began playing, the piano became silent; and when the Hindou had finished playing we heard again the sound of the piano - this illustrates a lesson, namely that when we listen to a most beautiful song, we must forget inferior music - when a lover of music has listened to the entrancing notes of a great master, his love of music will no longer be satisfied with the playing of the pupil.

Let us find out the melody, the sweet strains of which will be taken up by angels and carried to the supreme concourse - Let us hearken to a Melody which may stir the world of humanity - so that they may dance with joy - Let us listen to a strain which gives life to man- Then we can obtain universal results.

order.why: Distinguish the effects of words and melody in the brief recorded comparison.
Return to the connection between sound and spirit.
Read the reported relation of artistic gifts to inspiration.
Keep the recorded distinction between earthly and divine music.
Uses music and perfume to illustrate material things having spiritual effects.
Consider the reported aspiration to music that inspires peace.
Attend to the artist’s own encounter with meaning.
shortened: It has also been proven that the soul who summons the people to the Kingdom of God advances more rapidly and is more powerfully influenced than the hearers. The real artist is the one who feels every word and meaning of his song more, infinitely more than his audience.

order.why: Read the comparison between shipboard entertainment and heartfelt supplication.
Retain the separate recorded account of momentary pleasure.
Keep the reported call for influence beyond applause.
Distinguish passing emotion from the enduring solace envisioned by the text.
shortened: O nightingale of the rose-garden of God! Singing melodies will bring animation and happiness to the world of humanity, the hearers will be delighted and joyful and their deeper emotions stirred. But this gladness, this sense of emotion is transitory and will be forgotten within a short time. However, praise be to God, thou hast blended thy tunes with the melodies of the Kingdom, wilt impart solace to the world of the spirit and wilt everlastingly stimulate spiritual feelings.

order.why: Explore that distinction through natural and spiritual birdsong.
Read the contrast between outward excitement and devotion.
Hear the particular yearning for praise of the Beloved.
Preserve the recorded criticism of musical habits without making it an editorial judgment.
Read the reported celestial conservatory as a spiritual image.
Place renowned artists within a richly figurative invitation.
Retain the particular counsel on wise timing despite music’s permissibility.

shortened: The gathering of a large crowd, whether women or men, in one place and the rising of songs and melodies from the women causes agitation in the hearts of the enemies. The people of Iran are not yet able to tolerate such gatherings and songs and melodies.

order.why: Read the reported distinction between explicit text and future institutional guidance.
Preserve the recorded distinction between the Temple and nearby buildings.
shortened: There will be no organ in the Temple. In buildings nearby, festivals, services, conventions, public meetings and spiritual gatherings will be held, but in the Temple the chanting and singing will be unaccompanied.

order.why: Keep one reported vision of worship and its surrounding institutions.
shortened: When its accessories are completed and its full machinery starts running, when the melody of vocal and instrumental music arises and bursts upon the air with its joyous trends, when the prayers and supplications addressed at dawn and at sunrise ascend to the Throne of the Almighty, then will the effect of the Mashrekol-Azkar be made evident and manifest.

order.why: Retain the separate parallel account rather than merging identities.
shortened: When its accessories are completed and its full machinery starts running, when the melody of vocal and instrumental music arises and rends the air with its joyous trends, when the prayers and supplications addressed at dawn and at sunrise ascend to the throne of the Almighty,-then will the effect of the Mashrakol-Azkar be made evident and manifest.

order.why: Read the particular festival planned on the House of Worship grounds.
Include the brief recorded question and answer about songs in meetings.
Keep the reported acceptance of humble singing at a meeting’s end.
shortened: Meanwhile they may read some Tablets and Communes, and at the end of the meetings, if they desire to sing with the utmost supplication and meekness, it is acceptable.

order.why: Read the recorded preference for accessible beautiful songs when Persian is unavailable.
shortened: If there are those who have good voices, sing beautiful songs, if possible Persian chants and poems. If no one can do this in Persian, have sung any beautiful songs in English.

order.why: Include the encouragement to learn an Oriental tune.
Move toward sacred reading with voices joined.
Recognize a luminous gathering even without instruments.
shortened: Although outwardly there was no merriment or delight, and no musician played melodies and songs, and no harp or lute made music - there was no brimming cup, no joy-inducing wine, no ornament or adornment, no horn or flute - yet the holy and musk-laden breezes were wafting and the gathering of fellowship was radiant with light.

order.why: Read remembrance as the center of a gathering.
shortened: They must adorn their gathering with the remembrance of God and raise such melody and song as to bring the dwellers of the Kingdom into rapture and ecstasy.

order.why: Keep the plain description of a gathering in song.
shortened: When they arrange a gathering they sing sweet melodies and offer praise to the Lord of creation.

order.why: Aim performance toward others’ joy.
shortened: I hope that in the assemblies thou mayest sing praises with a sweet melody and thus become the cause of joy and gladness to all.

order.why: Recognize music’s contribution to fellowship.
shortened: In the days of God thou didst warble the most wondrous melodies in the garden of unity and opened thy lips in praise and glorification of the Lord. Thou wert the cause of joy and gladness to the friends of the All-Merciful and became the celestial musician in the spiritual gathering of fellowship.

order.why: Read singing as an ongoing service.
Include songs of communal love and harmony.
Extend the joy of festivities to friend and stranger.
Become harmonious companions in gratitude.
shortened: Therefore, it behooveth them to raise their heads to the stars and to be exalted to the zenith of eternal glory, to strike up a wondrous melody and to play upon the harp and lute, and in gratitude for the bounty of the peerless Lord to become harmonious companions.

order.why: Imagine many voices joined in praise.
shortened: Take up the harp and lute and raise a melody in harmony with the Supreme Concourse, that the birds of the meadow may come into rapture and ecstasy, and all may become engaged in one voice in praising and glorifying the Glorious Lord.

order.why: Keep the reported image of believers playing out of harmony.
Read the reported image of religions as instruments requiring harmony.
Preserve the particular women’s gathering and its music.
Join the education of women with their voices in devotion.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha's supreme joy is in observing that a number of leaves from among the handmaidens of the Blessed Beauty have been educated, that they are the essence of detachment, and are well-informed of the mysteries of the world of being; that they raise such a call in their glorification and praise of the Greatest Name as to cause the inmates of the Fanes of the Kingdom to become attracted and overjoyed, and that they recite prayers in prose and poetry, and melodiously chant the divine verses.

order.why: Welcome a daughter’s capacity to contribute to a gathering.
Read the prayer that a musical talent quicken hearts.
Preserve personal appreciation for a singer’s voice.
Read the praise of wisdom conveyed through melody.
shortened: O cherished friend! How fortunate thou wert to win the ball of precedence from the field of wisdom and to sing with celestial melody the divine mystery in the cosmic assembly with harp and lute.

order.why: Encounter a letter as a figurative symphony.
shortened: O Bashir-i-Ilahi! Thy letter was like unto a treasury of poems in glorification and praise of the Blessed Beauty. It hath imparted the utmost joy and gladness. Each word of thy letter is a sign of joyous music: One word is the lyre and the lute; another, the psalms of the House of David. One word is the timbrel and the harp; another, pure poetry and song. It is a perfect symphony, causing the listeners to leap with rapture and joy. From afar thou playest the melody, and here His lovers rejoice with ecstasy.

order.why: Hear beloved names described through musical refreshment.
Notice truths and meanings enjoyed in a sung text.
shortened: It was chanted and sung with the most wonderful melodies in the gathering of the friends. Hearts became joyful and souls were delighted by its truths and meanings.

order.why: Follow an appreciated poem into a new song.
Include chanting during a journey.
shortened: And on the way you would intone the blessed poems with marvelous melodies and adorn ears with their precious meanings.

order.why: Imagine a family sharing musical and spiritual culture.
Read the remembered music of a visit.
shortened: Thou wert present at the Threshold of Oneness, drank from the cup of grace, perfumed thy nostrils with the holy fragrances of the Blessed Spot, illumined thy face with the dust of God's threshold, and with melody, song, chanting, ecstasy, attraction and rapture watered the rose-garden and flower-bed of the Sacred Valley.

order.why: Hear a distant song as life and joy for others.
shortened: O sweet-singing bird! Your melody is in the mode of 'Iraq and Hijaz, and continuously reaches the Holy Land of the Self-Sufficing Lord. Your song gives life to souls and your melody brings joy to hearts.

order.why: Turn song toward praise and an avowal of servitude.
shortened: The ears of the Concourse on High hearken to thy melodies in glorification and praise, as thou extollest thy Lord, the Most Glorious.

Therefore, ascend to the Kingdom and warble like the dove of holiness in the gardens of the realm of might, glorifying the Lord of grandeur and the divine realm, the Most Glorious Luminary, and proclaiming my servitude to that exalted Threshold before which the Concourse on High bow down their radiant faces.

order.why: Retain the source’s unfinished musical blessing without inventing a terminator.
shortened: I swear by the Quintessence of existence that if thou shouldst attain this station thy voice shall be the voice of the Psalms of David, thy chanting shall echo with the melodies of holiness and sanctity in the path of the All- loving Lord

order.why: Read the psalms-of-David image as an aspiration to soften hearts.
Enter the extended metaphor of musical modes and the journey to the Beloved.
shortened: Since thou hast heard the sweet Hijazi melodies from the Iraqi Countenance, now hearken to the spiritual Shahnaz strains from the divine Falcon, that thou mayest perceive novel songs of faithfulness from the eternal lute and harp, and hear the melody of the divine pipe from the strike of the divine Unity, and step into the lane of the Beloved with all thy heart and soul, until thou becomest all spirit and fliest without wings, and art intoxicated without wine, and speakest eloquently without tongue, and attainest the stations of attraction, longing, ecstasy and taste, until thou forgettest sorrow and drinkest from the ocean of joy.

order.why: Consider the relation of modes, measures and capacity to hear.
Respond to verses with melodious recitation and thanks.
shortened: Thus have We sent down the verses and dispatched them unto thee that thou mayest recite them with melodious tunes and give thanks unto thy Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower.

order.why: Hear the surrounding world imagined as song.
Read servitude as playing to a divine call.
shortened: This is the time of profit and song, the moment for the melody of harp and lute.
Therefore we must all place the ring of His servitude in our ear and play to the melody of the divine call.

order.why: Invite every participant to take up a figurative instrument.
Allow song to arise from joy and remembrance.
shortened: In any case, spiritual wayfaring in the valley of divine love is greatly beloved, remembrance of God is acceptable, and singing songs and melodies out of intense joy and delight is desirable.

order.why: Sound the call to shared ecstasy and delight.
shortened: Take up the divine harp and strike up the melody of the Abha Kingdom, [saying]: "O Baha'is, show forth ecstasy and joy! O divine ones, seek attraction and rapture!"

order.why: Read the summons to move from silence into praise.
shortened: It is time for celestial music and the moment for the song of servitude at the Holy Threshold of His Holiness the Most Glorious. Why are you silent and quiet? Raise a cry, lift up your voice, sing melodies, strike the strings, raise high the song of praise to the Ancient Beauty and cry out in servitude to 'Abdu'l-Baha.

order.why: Keep the verse calling lifeless hearers to renewed life.
Imagine guidance as a rebeck stirring existence.
Read the bird-of-dawn address and its musical ambition.
Enter the feast where each voice contributes a melody.
Explore ever-new tunes that gladden heart and spirit.
shortened: In any case, always warble in the garden of divine knowledge with various melodies and novel tunes in praise of this servant's servitude, that the spirit may be stirred, the heart gladdened, the soul may find joy and delight, the lights of happiness may shine forth, and the bounty of joy may increase.
O nightingale! It is time for song and melody, the moment for harp and music.

order.why: Join dawn’s birds through musical harmony.
Preserve the observation of singers in public spaces in its particular context.
Recognize fluency and eloquence in a spiritual song.
shortened: O spiritual nightingale! You are ever engaged in melody and song, and in the rose-garden of inner meanings you raise your voice in hymns. The eloquence and fluency of your verses are clear and evident.

order.why: Read the aspiration to a gathering sustained through song.
Keep the distinct modes of Iraq and Hijaz in the appeal.
shortened: Let them sing with the accents of Iraq so that hearts may be moved and souls may be quickened; let them chant the melodies of Hijaz that all spirits may be animated by this divine vitality.

order.why: Bring instruments together in praise.
shortened: This prisoner's desire is that the friends arrange feasts of love and prepare celebrations of happiness, that they may experience perfect gladness through divine bounty and, through the grace of the Forgiving Lord, create gatherings of joy and delight. Let them play the lute and reed instrument, and harmonize with melodies of praise and glorification.

order.why: Read the repeated divine invocation as music.
Follow the extended sequence of modes, learning and spiritual stations.
Imagine a celebration prepared after distance and longing.
shortened: O ye who are inebriated with the draught of His Covenant! It is time to pass beyond the desolate wilds of remoteness, so that ye may reach the retreats of the Beloved, drink your fill from the wine of the bestowals of the All-Merciful, hold a heavenly festival, deck forth the stage for a spiritual celebration, and, to the strains of harp and lute and the melodies of the Concourse on high and the songsters in the meads of holiness, break into sweet lays and wondrous tunes in praise and glorification of the Abha Beauty.

order.why: Join instruments and assembly in love of God.
shortened: Like a lark bursting with gladness turn thy face towards the mystic rose garden at all times and sing the sweetest of thy songs. Strike on the cymbal, blow the trumpet, play the harpsichord with thy melodies, and gather in a beautiful assembly dedicated to the Love of God.

order.why: Retain the cultural explanation of nightingale imagery.
Set eloquent odes beside the variety of instruments.
Hear the invitation to begin composing and performing.
Keep the tavern imagery as part of the source’s devotional language.
Imagine the echo of a song crossing East and West.
shortened: Now return to the Orient and become an intimate companion and confidant of the merciful friends. Tune the harp of love and create a pleasing melody. Strike up a royal tune and raise such a song that its echo may reach both East and West.

order.why: Let the brief imperative renew the invitation to joy.
Preserve the quoted refrain and its allusion.
Read a personal encouragement away from lamentation toward song.
Keep the concise recognition of an ongoing melody.
Enter the heavenly assembly imagined as a place of renewing song.
Read the question about silence among known singers.
shortened: Despite the fact that the people of Kaf are famous for their singing and music and melodies and stations of bayat and hijaz modes and Iraqi rhythms, what happened that you became completely silent and lifeless and intoxicated and bewildered?

order.why: Imagine gatherings across the earth joining in praise.
shortened: In every spot on the face of the earth, gatherings of the loved ones are organized and arranged, and the melody of the lute and string and song is raised with "Glory be to God!" and "God is Most Great!", and the song of the Concourse on High reaches the ears of both the noble and the lowly.

order.why: Hear the aspiration to a melody that moves creation.
shortened: May they strike up such a melody that its fame spreads throughout the world and sing such a song that moves the kingdom of creation.

order.why: Invite each person into the role of musician.
shortened: Let each become a wondrous musician, tune the harp of the Most Great Glad-Tidings, and with lute and string begin the melody of the love of God.

order.why: Read the exuberant imagery of song drawing hidden souls outward.
shortened: Therefore raise the song of joy and lift up the melody of delight, and with lute and lyre engage in singing and chanting with the utmost ecstasy and rapture until the dwellers in the cloisters of the Kingdom are moved to joy and delight and the recluses in the retreat of the Lord of the Realm of Might cast aside their veils and hasten to the plain of manifestation.

order.why: Connect continual thanksgiving with music.
shortened: At every moment offer thanks and praise, and with harp and melody raise a song and tune until you set the world in motion and make souls the confidants and companions of the Concourse on High.

order.why: Keep the text’s energetic picture of a spiritual gathering.
shortened: They must adorn spiritual gatherings, chant songs and strike up melodies and anthems to bring the listeners into a state of joy and ecstasy, that they may hear the praise of the Concourse on High and witness the glorification of the people of the Most Glorious Kingdom, and hear the divine melody from the horizon of grandeur, becoming wonderstruck and transported, and dancing and leaping with the utmost joy and gladness, sacrificing their lives.

order.why: Pray for joy expressed in movement and gratitude.

Read the declared season of song and its dependence on raised voices.
Consider the melody described as an opening to mysteries.
Bring instruments and an ode of servitude into shared happiness.
shortened: With harp and drum and reed and strings, in the gathering of the righteous ones, compose melodies and songs of mysteries with the utmost joy and enthusiasm, and chant and recite this ode of servitude's contents so that the doors of happiness and joy may be opened to the hearts of the people of God and to this 'Abdu'l-Baha.

order.why: Return to the joining of earthly and heavenly music.
shortened: When the earthly music is joined with the heavenly music such happiness and acclamation become revealed in the hearts that the spirits will soar heavenward.

order.why: Read the wish that music become a source of life.
Explore the chords of meanings through Davidic imagery.
Keep the exuberant poetic account of joy and dancing.
Read meaningful melodies as teaching spiritual stations.
shortened: Today is the day of the divine call and the voice is the voice of God, so that the birds of the gardens of unity may, in the rose-garden of detachment, teach lessons of spiritual stations with meaningful melodies, and may become engaged in singing and chanting upon the branches of existence with the psalms of the House of David.

order.why: Situate a particular song within the Ridvan festival.
shortened: O spiritual nightingale, sing a melody with the divine sweet tone on this Ridvan Festival in praise and glorification of the All-Merciful Beauty, that the song of "O Glory of the Most Glorious" may reach the ears of this servant.

order.why: Pray for a voice wholly turned toward joy.
shortened: O thou maidservant of God! I hope that thou wilt attain to great enthusiasm and rapture; that thou wilt wholly turn into an eloquent tongue, and thou wilt, with perfect joy, play on thy harp and raise its melody in this Heavenly Rose-Garden.

order.why: Keep the source’s comparison between sung devotion and instruments.
Devote life and voice to attracting hearts.
Imagine each breath carrying a call to inattentive listeners.
Read the heightened poetic gesture of a singer in the gathering.
shortened: Therefore, with rent garment, disheveled hair and glowing countenance, sing love songs in the gathering of the friends, raise spiritual melodies and lift up the anthem of the Abha Kingdom, that thou mayest move the world of being and bring joy and gladness to the Concourse on High.

order.why: Invite music that revives hearts.
Preserve the movement among musical modes and moods.
Welcome a familiar song alongside the many calls for novelty.
shortened: Thou must come with the old song, so that the melodies and harmonies may impart the utmost joy and fragrance.

order.why: Read the invitation to a Persian bird to begin again.
Imagine a voice prompting others to answer.
Recognize the performer’s place in the feast of worship.
Join composition with an aspiration to discover meaning.
Distinguish the song that communicates inner realities.
Offer the garden’s invitation to every singing bird.
Connect musical development with progress, culture and release from status.
Bring Barbad and David together in the imagery of a gathering.
shortened: In gatherings and meetings, play and sing with the melody of Barbad and the psalms of David, that the angels of the Supreme Concourse may experience joy and delight and obtain spiritual happiness.

order.why: Read the resolve to hold a gathering and raise its song.
Preserve the reported banquet with its varied instruments and singers.
Hear the recorded comparison of a cheering song to a ray of the sun.
shortened: This song cheered me, for it proved to be a strain of the music of the Supreme Kingdom, an anthem which connotes that of heaven, and a refrain indicative of the divine, even as a ray of the sun is indicative of the sun. It is just as a strain cheers the heart that anthem of the Kingdom moves the heart of existence.

order.why: Keep the reported therapeutic claim attributed to its conversation.
Retain the recorded account of music as the heart’s language.
shortened: In this great dispensation music is one of the arts that is highly approved and is considered to be the cause of the exaltation of sad and despondent hearts.
Music is most important. Music is the heart's own language. Its vibrations uplift the spirit; it is very beautiful and a great art.

order.why: Close the source-linked readings with a prayer for an attuned voice.
Widen the supplied readings toward arts in villages, towns and cities.
End with the capacity of artistic expression to awaken noble sentiment.

questions: What experiences help you understand the image of music as a ladder for the soul?
How do a performer’s intention, the meaning of a text, and a listener’s state of mind interact in a musical experience?
What would it mean to take both artistic excellence and spiritual purpose seriously in teaching children music?
How can a community welcome unfamiliar musical traditions while remaining attentive to the purpose of a gathering?
Which passages concern musical practice, and which use music as an image for spiritual life; how do those uses illuminate one another?
What might allow the joy of a song to grow into lasting fellowship, service, or a changed way of listening?
