subjects.displayTitle: A call to the world: hearing, fairness, and the promise of renewal
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh addressed the peoples of the earth from a prison cell. That contrast runs through the whole of His summons: the Wronged One in ‘Akká, confined in the most desolate of cities, speaks as the Lord of Names and announces that He Whom the Books promised has come to reform the world and refine its nations. He asks first for something modest. Adorn yourselves with tranquility and dignity, He says; cast aside tyranny and look with the eye of fairness; judge for yourselves what has been sent down. Only then come the great images: gates flung open, a sun rising, living water offered without price, a Book that speaks, earth and sea and clouds bearing witness to the Day. Isaiah’s invitation to come to the waters belongs beside them, bounty freely given that still asks a changed life in return. The call presses one question on every listener: what makes hearing possible, and which inherited allegiance or treasured possession stands in the way? From here the same voice turns to the kings and rulers and to the divines of every faith, and the announcement becomes a call to action in the conduct of ordinary days.
subjects.arc: Begin with fair judgment and the purpose of reform; hear the proclamation from confinement; explore promise, renewal and obstacles to recognition; turn finally toward gratitude and action.

order.why: Offer the ocean of wisdom as an inviting image.
shortened: O peoples of the world! Cast away, in My name that transcendeth all other names, the things ye possess, and immerse yourselves in this Ocean in whose depths lay hidden the pearls of wisdom and of utterance, an ocean that surgeth in My name, the All-Merciful.

order.why: Open with tranquility and dignity as a way of approaching the subject.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! Adorn your temples with the ornament of tranquility and dignity.

order.why: Connect glad tidings with an end to strife and a purpose of reform.
Ask for the abandonment of tyranny and an eye of fairness.
shortened: Say: O concourse of men! Fear God and follow not your idle fancies. By God! He Who was promised in the Books of God and mentioned in the hearts of the Messengers hath come. Cast aside tyranny, then look with the eye of fairness at that which hath been sent down from God, the Ancient Revealer.

order.why: Make fair judgment explicit before exploring claims.
Invite reflection on the standard by which a claim is judged.
shortened: Say: Be fair, O people! If ye deny Him, by what path will ye approach and to what command will ye hold fast? By God! They have no protector save that they repent and return unto God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: State the announced purpose of reforming the world and refining nations.
shortened: O concourse of men! He Who was promised in the Books of God hath come, He Whose remembrance was treasured in the hearts of the Messengers. He hath come to reform the world and refine the nations.

order.why: Introduce a summons that asks for no recompense.
Locate the invitation to behold and listen in a prison.
Hear the Wronged One’s call from confinement.
Place imprisonment beside the stated purpose of salvation.
Retain the plea that opposition not become violence or dissension.
Recognize remembrance of others amid sorrow.
shortened: O people of the earth! We make mention of you at a time when sorrows have encompassed Us through that which the hands of the deniers of this blessed and manifest Light have wrought.

order.why: Trace the call across the named places of its history.
Locate the call specifically in Akka.
Hear the invitation from the Prison in Akka in its own brief form.
shortened: O concourse of creation! Hearken unto that which the Lord of Names proclaimeth from His Prison in 'Akka.

order.why: Preserve the source’s theological claim about the imprisoned speaker.
Read the prison call as drawing listeners near to God.
Attend to the warning that inherited allegiance can obstruct hearing.
Answer the call with a radiant face.
Keep the Mother Book’s prison address and its warning in context.
shortened: The Mother Book from the horizon of the Prison's heaven calls out and says: O people of the earth! Fear the All-Merciful and follow not the desires of those who have disbelieved in God and His signs, and have broken His Covenant, and have pronounced against Him with manifest injustice.

order.why: Hear the repeated invitation of the Beloved from the Most Great Prison.
shortened: The fragrance of the garment has wafted, and the Kingdom of holiness has appeared, and the Beloved of the world calls out from His Most Great Prison: "To Me, to Me, O peoples of earth and heaven! To Me, to Me, O ye who dwell in the Kingdom of names!"

order.why: Connect confinement with the image of a most manifest ocean and light.
shortened: On this day the Wronged One calleth out from the Most Great Prison unto the peoples of the world and summoneth them unto the Most Great Ocean. His Cause is more manifest than the sun and His utterance is as the rays of light.

order.why: Invite a listener through wisdom and utterance.
Repeat the invitation to come and hear through a different address.
shortened: Take hold of the Book of God with the power that proceeds from Him and say: O peoples of the earth, come ye, come ye, that I may cause you to hear the call of God and show you His Supreme Horizon.

order.why: Ask what it means for a hidden treasury of knowledge to be shown.
shortened: Come ye, that I may show you the lights of God from this luminous horizon. That which lay concealed in the treasuries of knowledge hath been made manifest, and He Who was promised throughout the ages and centuries hath come.

order.why: Approach an opened gate with humility.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! The gate of divine generosity hath been opened in the Most Great Scene - turn ye unto it with humility and repentance.

order.why: Preserve the bracketed context in the brief announcement of the Gate.
Read the Bab’s reported call to awaken and prepare the way.
shortened: Raise the cry: "Awake, awake, for, lo! the Gate of God is open, and the morning Light is shedding its radiance upon all mankind! The promised One is made manifest; prepare the way for Him, O people of the earth! Deprive not yourselves of its redeeming grace, nor close your eyes to its effulgent glory."

order.why: Keep the distinct reported declaration at Tabriz and its source omission.
shortened: Verily I say, it is incumbent upon the peoples of both the East and the West to obey My word and to pledge allegiance to My person.

order.why: Emphasize the stated worldwide reach of the summons.
Read the concise affirmation that the announcement has gone to all.
shortened: We have given glad tidings of this most mighty, most holy Cause and this most glorious, most exalted Revelation to all the world.

order.why: Extend the summons to the whole realm of creation.
shortened: He calleth out with the most exalted call between earth and heaven, summoning all who dwell in the realm of creation to the supreme horizon.

order.why: Hear the epistle explicitly addressed to all earth’s inhabitants.
Include the invitation to both young and old.
shortened: Convey My greetings unto them and give them the glad-tidings of this Book which speaketh with truth between the heavens and the earth, that by God, the Manifestation of Revelation hath come and calleth out in the most exalted voice to all, young and old, inviting all to the supreme Paradise, that station wherein the Sadratu'l-Muntaha proclaimeth: The kingdom belongeth to God, the One, the All-Informed.

order.why: Address all religions in the language of promise and gratitude.
shortened: When We desired to make mention of thee, the ocean of utterance surged, and the Tongue of Grandeur spoke in the Kingdom of knowledge: "O peoples of all religions! Turn ye unto that which ye were promised by the Most Exalted Pen of God, then give thanks unto your Lord, the Compassionate, the Generous. He hath manifested Himself and fulfilled His promise through His grace, and He is the All-Bountiful, the All-Knowing."

order.why: Read the Mother Book and Balance addressing religious communities.
shortened: By God! This is the Day whereon the Mother Book speaketh and the Balance proclaimeth among all possibilities: O peoples of all religions! The Promised One hath come and through Him the horizon of the world is illumined. Turn ye unto Him and be not of the heedless ones.

order.why: Pause at the compact claim concerning the Lord of all religions.
shortened: O concourse of men! The Lord of all religions hath come.

order.why: Develop that claim through the appeal to Scriptures and Tablets.
Consider attachment to what one possesses within a religious community.
Read fulfillment named across Psalms and Tablets.
shortened: Say: Fear God, O peoples of the earth! He Who was promised in the Psalms and Tablets has come, He Who was mentioned in the Scriptures of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Connect the promised and the formerly hidden.
Preserve the claim that the Messengers heralded this appearance.
Notice the contrast between a fulfilled promise and continuing darkness.
shortened: O people of creation! He Who was mentioned in the Books of God, the Lord of the worlds, the Sovereign of heaven, hath come. The Day is come, but the people are in manifest darkness.

order.why: Hear the announcement spoken while walking.
Read appointed time and remembrance in sacred books together.
shortened: Say: O people! By God the Truth, the appointed time is fulfilled and the All-Bestowing One is come, through Whose remembrance every book and scroll and preserved tablet hath been adorned.

order.why: Call a recipient to give voice to the announced fulfillment.
shortened: Arise and say: O peoples of the earth! The Day hath come wherein God hath fulfilled His promise, such that He hath manifested Him Whose mention was hidden in knowledge and concealed from eyes and sight.

order.why: Consider what was treasured in the Books now described as manifest.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! By God, the Hidden One has come and what was treasured in the Books of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, has been made manifest.

order.why: Read the invitation to receive what the texts claim was concealed.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! The Promised One hath appeared and made manifest that which lay concealed in the Books of God and treasured within His all-encompassing knowledge. Cast away what ye possess and take hold of that which hath been sent down from the heaven of the will of your Lord, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Keep the tension between a promised meeting and rejection.
Read the question about denying what had been promised.
shortened: Say: O people! Do ye deny that which ye were promised? Fear God and be not of them whom We behold in doubt and schism. This is the Promised One Who hath come from the dawning-place of the Promise with proof and evidence.

order.why: Let paired questions about understanding and sight sharpen that tension.
shortened: Say: O people! Ye have been promised in the Tablets this Manifestation. Now hath He appeared with truth - wherefore do ye not understand? And He Whom ye were promised by the tongue of truth hath now come with truth - wherefore do ye not see?

order.why: Ask on what proof a refusal rests.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the earth! Why do ye not arise from your seats, and by what proof have ye turned away from Him Who was promised in the Book?

order.why: Consider hearing and seeing without recognizing.
Set the illumination described by the text beside the doubts of nations.
shortened: O people of earth and heaven! By God, He hath come through whom the eye of the world is illumined, yet the nations are in manifest doubt.

order.why: Preserve the ongoing call despite turning away.
shortened: O concourse of the earth! By God, the Promise hath come to pass and the Promised One hath appeared with manifest sovereignty, calling out to mankind in all conditions while they turn away from the Truth and follow every heedless doubter.

order.why: Read the caution against allowing others’ rejection to determine response.
Consider the historical example of Muhammad’s reception.
Address religious scholars with the invitation not to miss a bounty.
shortened: Say: O concourse of divines! Fear the Lord of Names. He has come with verses that have attracted the hearts of those who know. Beware lest ye deprive yourselves of this bounty which has encompassed the seen and unseen.

order.why: Keep the polemical account of religious opposition attributed to its source.
shortened: He speaketh and uttereth: O people of the earth! The Lord of Heaven hath come with the Kingdom of Names, through His Most Glorious Name, whereby the Concourse on High rejoiced and every wearer of a white turban lamented - they who seized upon idle fancies and cast certainty behind their backs, following their own desires.

order.why: Read the specific appeal to the Day mentioned in the Qur’an.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the earth! By God, this is the Day whose mention was sent down in the Qur'an, the Day when mankind shall stand before the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Link fulfilled promise to the One who spoke on Sinai.
shortened: And in it He hath fulfilled His promise and manifested His sovereignty and proclaimed before the faces of the world: "O people! The Promised One hath come! He is verily the One Who spoke on Sinai.

order.why: Hear the Lote-Tree’s declaration through Sinai imagery.
Read the fire of the Tree on the Mount of Knowledge.
shortened: O people of the world! The Light of the Ancient One is shining from the horizon of the heaven of the Most Great Name, and the Fire of the Tree is blazing and speaking forth on the Mount of Knowledge.

order.why: Connect hearing with the Tree of the Uttermost Boundary.
Keep one version of the Mount’s announcement and resurrection imagery.
shortened: This is the Day whereon the Most Great Name calleth aloud amidst the nations and giveth them glad tidings of this Manifestation, at Whose appearance the Mount spoke forth saying: "He Who was promised hath come, through Him the Hidden One hath been revealed, and those who lay in their graves have arisen."

order.why: Preserve the separately sourced parallel rather than conflating it.
shortened: This is the Day whereon the Most Great Name calleth aloud among the nations and giveth them glad tidings of this Manifestation, at Whose appearance the Mount declared: "The Promised One hath come, and through Him the Hidden One hath been revealed, and those in the graves have arisen."

order.why: Read the Hour and Resurrection as voices of glad tidings.
shortened: The world hath been adorned with the ornament of the Ancient King, and longing hath seized all regions, yet most of the people are in manifest denial. The Word hath appeared and the Hour hath called out, and the Resurrection proclaimeth: "Glad tidings unto you, O concourse of the earth, in this blessed and wondrous Day!"

order.why: Invite a recipient to announce the Hour with vision.
shortened: The Most Holy, Most Great, Most Glorious Book from Us to him who hath turned towards the Dawning-Place of Revelation when the horizon of utterance was illumined with the Sun of wisdom and exposition, that he may inhale the fragrances of the verses in the days of his Lord, the Almighty, the Mighty, the Bestower, and may arise amidst the servants in the name of his Lord, the Possessor of all being, saying: "O people! The Hour hath come and the Resurrection hath appeared. Blessed are they who are endued with vision."

order.why: Preserve the startling images of cleft heaven and moving mountains.
Read the revelation of proof alongside smoke and a changed heaven.
shortened: Say: By God! The All-Merciful hath come with such a proof as all who are in the heavens and on earth cannot withstand, did ye but know. Take hold of God's Tablet and detach thyself from all else. Say: O people! This is a Day wherein the Beauty of the Self-Subsisting hath appeared, the heaven hath been cleft asunder, and the smoke hath enveloped all in the realm of possibility save those who have turned toward the Most Sublime Vision.

order.why: Bring fairness back into the account of smoke and salvation.
Connect the new Day with movement from darkness into light.
shortened: Say: Today He hath appeared in truth, and none have understood save those possessed of insight. This is the Day whereof We gave you tidings aforetime through Our true utterance: "Lead mankind out of darkness into light and give them glad-tidings of the days of God, the Almighty, the All-Powerful, the Unconstrained."

order.why: Listen to leaves, trees and heaven as witnesses.
shortened: Verily the leaves do speak: "The Daystar of the horizons hath appeared!" And the trees do cry aloud: "The Chosen One hath appeared!" And the heaven doth proclaim: "The Lord of Names hath come!"

order.why: Hear earth itself speak in the proclamation.
Let sea and land join the account of the promised Day.
shortened: O people! The sea is walking and beareth witness unto the Promised One, and the land proclaimeth: The Day hath come, and dominion belongeth unto God, the Mighty, the Loving.

order.why: Read the sea’s blessing of dry land and the call to release grief.
shortened: He heareth and seeth, and He is the Mighty, the Glorious, the Best-Beloved. O people! Remember your Lord, the All-Merciful, and follow not every ignorant outcast. This is a Day wherein the Ocean saith to the dry land: Blessed art thou, since God hath honored thee with His footsteps. O concourse of earth! Grieve not for aught, for by God, the Promise hath come, and this is the Promised One Who walketh in the mansion and calleth all unto God, the Mighty, the Loving.

order.why: Hear the clouds proclaim sovereignty.
shortened: Verily the clouds cry out with the most exalted call between earth and heaven: "O people! By God, the All-Bestowing One hath come with a sovereignty before which neither the hosts of the heavens nor of the earth can stand. Fear ye God and be not of the wrongdoers.

order.why: Receive rain, opened gates and illuminated horizons together.
shortened: Say: O people! The gates of heaven have been opened, the clouds pour down their rain, and the horizons are illumined. Cast aside what ye possess and turn unto Him Who calleth you to a station that transcendeth all mention.

order.why: Listen to the bird of the throne announcing an unveiled Beloved.
shortened: The Ancient Beauty hath ascended the throne of His Most Great Name, and the bird of the throne is warbling in the sweetest of tones and the most wondrous of melodies in His presence, proclaiming, "O concourse of earth and heaven! Rejoice, for the veil hath been rent asunder and the covering torn away, and the face of the Beloved hath shone forth above the horizon of power with a sovereignty that neither the ascendancy of the wicked nor the clamour of the boastful can thwart. Bestir yourselves and hasten with all your hearts to the presence of your Beloved.

order.why: Keep the Cock of the Throne and the text’s strong claim about manifestation.
shortened: The Cock of the Throne has crowed at the settling of the All-Merciful upon the thrones of possibility. O heedless ones! The Lord of Names has come and My manifestation with grandeur and power is more excellent than the worship of all created things and that which the Daysprings of Names, the dwellers in the cities of eternity, and the Concourse on High have done.

order.why: Imagine all creation seized by the rapture of revelation.
shortened: This is the Day wherein the rapture of divine revelation hath taken hold of all created things, the Day wherein He Who had been mentioned in the books of God, the All-Glorious, the All-Wise, hath been made manifest.

order.why: Read the suns, tablets and hands as images of disclosed power.
shortened: Say: O people! The Suns of eternity have shone forth from the Most Glorious Horizon, and the Command hath been detailed in the Tablets of Destiny, and the Hands of Power have emerged from the sleeves.

order.why: Connect fragrance, Word and Herald in one announcement.
Hear Light proclaim what the Books foretold.
shortened: Verily the Light hath shone forth in this hour from Mine evident horizon and hath called out with the most exalted call, saying: "O people of the realm of creation! That which was spoken of in the Books of God hath appeared, and He for Whose manifestation and advent the worlds were created hath come.

order.why: Preserve the brief source announcement that all things proclaim the Sovereign.
Consider earth honored by an advent.
shortened: O people of the earth! By God, the Lord of heaven hath come with manifest sovereignty. The earth hath been honored by His advent, would ye but understand.

order.why: Read illuminated peaks against human heedlessness.
shortened: O people of the earth! That which was concealed in the eternity of eternities hath appeared, and by its lights have the peaks and mountains been illumined, while ye remain among the heedless.

order.why: Pass from days and names toward inner meanings.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! Cast aside the days and names. The Day of God hath come with a light by which the heavens and earths were illumined. Turn ye toward the ocean of meanings by the command of One mighty and powerful.

order.why: Hear the Day announced in the Book of Existence.
Read Day and Book as linked claims.
shortened: Say: O people! By God, this is the Day of God, were ye of them that know, and this is the Book of God which had been inscribed from all eternity, were ye of them that are assured.

order.why: Consider the Book appearing in human temple.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! By God, verily the Book hath appeared in the temple of man and announceth unto you the appearance of God and His sovereignty. Hearken ye, and be not of the heedless.

order.why: Read the creative force assigned to a single letter.
Preserve the source’s claim of signs throughout the human form.
Join personal remembrance with the Hidden Book and Treasured Mystery.
Consider the Key as an image of disclosure.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the earth! The Most Great Key hath appeared and that which was hidden in God's knowledge hath been revealed, and I am the All-Seeing Witness.

order.why: Read the concise pairing of promised advent and revealed mystery.
shortened: Say: O people! The Promised One hath come unto you, if ye be of them that know, and the Hidden Mystery hath been revealed, if ye be of the certain ones.

order.why: Hear the announcement from the Mount of knowledge.
shortened: The Luminous Beauty has turned toward the Mount of knowledge, and upon reaching its highest station spoke these words: "O concourse of humanity! Fear God, the Lord of destiny. He Who was hidden from all eyes and concealed in all hearts has appeared.

order.why: Combine manifest sovereignty with an opened treasury.
shortened: He calleth out at all times: O concourse of possibilities! By God, the All-Merciful hath appeared with a sovereignty that hath subdued all who are in the heavens and on earth. O people! By God, the Most Great Spectacle hath appeared and the Lord of Destiny proclaimeth with His most exalted Call: This is the Day wherein what was hidden in the Treasury of God, the Mighty, the Inaccessible, hath been revealed.

order.why: Receive the Day described as bounty.
shortened: Say: O concourse of creation! This is the Day of Bounty when the Creator of the heavens hath come with the kingdom of names.

order.why: Remember the appearance as a favor.
Hear the simple offer of glad tidings.
shortened: O people of the world! The Ancient Lord Who hath manifested Himself through the Most Great Name bringeth you glad tidings.

order.why: Read the surging seas and fragrance as signs of bounty.
shortened: We have sent down for thee that which hath caused the seas to surge and the fragrance of God, the Lord of the beginning and the end, to waft abroad. Say: O people! The Self-Subsisting is come, and the command is God's, the Almighty, the Unconstrained. Beware lest ye deprive yourselves of this most great bounty. Cast away what the people possess and take what ye are bidden by God, Who illumineth the horizons.

order.why: Keep the specific announcement of glad tidings from the horizon.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! By God, the Promise hath come, and He Who was promised calleth unto you from His most exalted horizon and giveth you glad tidings of that which hath dawned and shone forth from the horizon of the will of your Lord, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.

order.why: Respond to the fulfilled promise with praise.
shortened: O peoples of the earth, hearken unto My call and be not of the heedless ones. The promise hath come to pass and the Truth hath appeared - praise ye God for this great bounty.

order.why: Consider the worth assigned to these days and the invitation to thankfulness.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! Fear God, and deny not My proof, and dispute not My verses, and reject not My favor which We have sent down from the heaven of My mercy. Thus doth My Most Exalted Pen counsel you on this darksome night. Hearken, and be not among the heedless. Know ye the worth of these days and their station. God hath made their lights from the light of His countenance and their radiance from the sun of His grace, that ye may give thanks unto your Lord, the All-Bountiful, the Most Generous.

order.why: Pause at the warning against depriving oneself.
shortened: O people! The Self-Subsisting hath come and saith: Beware, O peoples of the earth, lest ye deprive yourselves. The Beauty hath shone forth from the horizon of glory - turn ye toward Him with your hearts.

order.why: Read the lament that one who comes for life is opposed.
shortened: This is a Tablet that lamenteth and saith: O people! Oppose not Him Who hath come for your life, and turn not away from Him to Whom the All-Merciful hath testified in all conditions that He is the Goal of all worlds.

order.why: Explore the image of the world’s pulse in a Physician’s hand.
shortened: Say: O concourse of nations! From whom do ye flee this Day? By God! The Ancient Source hath appeared and in His hand is the pulse of the world. He healeth it as He pleaseth, and verily He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. Say: Do ye flee from Him Who hath come unto you with the Kawthar of everlasting life? Fear ye the All-Merciful, and be not of those who have disbelieved in God, the Lord of lords.

order.why: Imagine hearing as guidance and a draught of recognition.
Follow the imagery of life, water, wine and grateful recognition.
Read the raised pavilion as a place of bounty.
shortened: The pavilion of bounty hath been raised aloft, and the Lord of Eternity summoneth the peoples unto the Most Exalted Horizon which hath been illumined by the lights of His Most Glorious Name.

order.why: Hear the chalice call hearts and souls to hasten.
shortened: This is the Day wherein the chalice of bounty proclaimeth: "Come ye! Come ye! Hasten! Hasten, O dwellers of earth, with your hearts and souls!"

order.why: Attend to favors described as descending from heaven.
shortened: Turn to Him, O people of the earth, then hearken to what descends from the heaven of His all-encompassing favors upon the worlds.

order.why: Make turning with the heart the immediate response.
Read the call to the Lord of Eternity.
shortened: O peoples of the world! The Lord of Eternity hath come with His Most Great Name and calleth you unto Him, if ye be of them that hearken.

order.why: Keep the distinct brief invitation to hearken.
shortened: O peoples of the world! Hearken unto the call of the Lord of eternity. He, verily, commandeth you to observe righteousness and God-consciousness, and acquainteth you with that which shall profit you throughout the eternity of God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Let the plain address to earth’s dwellers stand on its own.
shortened: O dwellers of earth! Hearken unto the call of your Lord, the Lord of all beings. He calleth you from the precincts of His Most Great Prison and remindeth you of the signs of God and His days.

order.why: Hear the short warning against inattentiveness.
shortened: O people of the earth! Hearken unto the Call, and be not of the heedless ones. Raise up your heads from the couch of heedlessness and desire.

order.why: Consider the Day of Hearing as a name for the moment.
Read the speaking Book and the blessing of receptive ear and eye.
Recognize the stated purpose of guidance.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the earth! By God, He hath appeared Who summoneth all unto God, the Lord of existence, and He hath come Who guideth all to the outstretched path of God.

order.why: Hear the announcement of what is ordained for people.
Retain the explicit declaration of divine unity.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! Hearken unto that which the Lord of Destiny proclaimeth from the Most Great Scene: "There is none other God but I, the Almighty, the All-Powerful."

order.why: Keep the separate proclamation of that unity and grace.
shortened: O peoples of the world! Hearken unto the call of God, the Sovereign of eternity. Verily, there is none other God but Me, the Mighty, the Gracious.

order.why: Read the promised Day’s confession of divine unity.
shortened: The Day of the Promise is come, and He Who is the Promised One loudly proclaimeth before all who are in heaven and all who are on earth, 'Verily there is none other God but He, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting!'

order.why: Hear the proclamation placed at the heart of the world.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! Hearken unto the call of Him Who is the Fashioner of the heavens, Who hath come with the Kingdom of Names. He speaketh at the heart of the world and summoneth all unto His Most Great Name, through which all things proclaimed when it was made manifest: "The Promised One hath come with His All-Compelling Name and hath spoken: 'There is none other God but Me, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.'"

order.why: Imagine all things proclaiming a kingdom.
Let the Pen give voice to the Ancient King’s coming.
shortened: The Most Pure, the Most Glorious! The Pen calleth out to all peoples: "He Who is the Ancient King hath come! The Kingdom is God's, the Almighty, the Unconstrained!"

order.why: Preserve the distinct declaration of the Most Exalted Pen.
shortened: And the Most Exalted Pen declareth: 'O peoples of creation! By God, the Lord of Names and Creator of the heavens hath come! Turn ye unto Him, and be not of those who have denied God's proof and His signs, if ye be understanding.

order.why: Read heaven’s declaration of sovereignty over meaning and utterance.
Consider the claim of sovereignty beyond circumstances.
shortened: Verily the Tablet proclaimeth with the most exalted call, saying: O concourse of creation! By God, the Lord of Names hath come with a sovereignty that the circumstances of creation cannot prevent nor can intimations veil.

order.why: Retain the assertion that human affairs cannot frustrate this call.
Read the claim of a Cause beyond combined earthly force.
Preserve the further account of all-encompassing sovereignty.
shortened: O people of the world! By God the Truth, the All-Merciful has come with a sovereignty that has encompassed all who are in the heavens and earth, and with a Cause before which neither the world nor any of its peoples can stand.

order.why: Hear the declared commission and evidence.
Connect opened heaven with the Lord riding on clouds.
Read guidance through banners on lofty mountains.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! By God, God hath come with His glory, and the banners of guidance have been raised upon every lofty and exalted mountain.

order.why: Keep the call toward the Supreme Horizon.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! The Most Great Name hath come, calling you unto the Supreme Horizon. Fear ye the Lord of all beings, and be not of the heedless ones.

order.why: Hear the invitation through a kingdom of verses.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! The Lord of Heaven hath come with His kingdom of verses - turn ye unto Him, and be not of the heedless.

order.why: Read the Most Great News alongside the invitation to follow the Revealer.
Consider the claim that proof has been perfected.
shortened: Say: O people! He Who is the Intended One hath appeared and the proof hath been perfected. Hold fast unto God and follow not every ignorant remote one.

order.why: Read recognition as the significance of the Day of proof.
shortened: O concourse of men! The Lord of Destiny remembereth you from the direction of His Most Great Scene. Draw nigh and be not of them that hesitate. This is the Day of proof, were ye of them that know, and this is the Day of recognition, were ye of them that are certain.

order.why: Return to fairness within the question of sovereignty.
shortened: Say: O people of the earth, be fair in the Cause of God and His sovereignty, and follow not the desires of those who have denied the Witness and the Witnessed.

order.why: Judge the described light fairly while considering attachment to possessions.
shortened: Say: O people, be fair in your judgment regarding this Light through which the worlds of inner meaning and utterance have been illumined, and through which the door of divine presence hath been opened before all who are in earth and heaven, and the Dove of Utterance hath warbled upon the highest branch of divine knowledge.
Say: That which ye possess will profit you not this Day.

order.why: Read the challenge to bring a greater proof in its polemical setting.
Let the appeal to fairness address doubts about light and signs.
shortened: O thou who speaketh in My Name! Say: O people of the earth! Do ye doubt God, or this Light whereby the heavens and earth were illumined, or His signs which have filled the horizons? Say: Be fair, O people, and follow not those who have denied God, the Lord of all names.

order.why: Ask what remains to hold fast to when a claim is rejected.
shortened: Say: O people! Rend asunder the veils - this is your Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower. By God! The promise hath appeared and the Promised One hath come with manifest sovereignty. If ye disbelieve, by what thing will ye hold fast?

order.why: Retain the text’s strong call to turn to the Dayspring of verses.
Consider the contrast drawn between following desire and following proof.
shortened: Say: O people of the earth! Fear ye God, and follow not your desires. Follow Him Who hath come unto you with the kingdom of proof from the All-Merciful.

order.why: Use remembrance as the text’s image for burning obstructive desires.
shortened: O people! The proof hath come, and He Who revealeth the utterance hath appeared with a manifest sovereignty. Follow not your desires - burn them with the fire of the remembrance of your Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Consider the call to break idols of imagination.
shortened: Say: O people of the earth! Fear God and follow not those whom veils have prevented from the Source of verses. Break the idols of fancy and imagination in the name of your Lord, the Possessor of all names.

order.why: Read the invitation to relinquish fancies.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the earth! Cast away what ye possess of idle fancies and vain imaginings. Take hold of that which ye have been commanded by God, the Revealer of verses.

order.why: Turn from fancies toward certitude.
shortened: O people! Cast aside your idle fancies and turn toward the Dayspring of certitude. Thus doth the All-Merciful command you, if ye be of them that know.

order.why: Read the summons to answer without mistaking its imperative for a question-and-answer label.
shortened: O people! Answer Him Who calleth you unto God, then cast away what ye possess of idle fancies. The Sun of Certitude hath dawned with a radiance that no veils of the world can withhold.

order.why: Keep the warning about unexamined allegiance to a clamorous voice.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! Fear ye God, and follow not every remote clamourer who hath cast away righteousness and taken up passion in following the imaginings of the heedless.

order.why: Preserve the warning against following those described as denying the proof.
Read the obstacle of worldly vanities.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! Fear God and follow not those whom the world hath deluded with its vanities in such wise as to have debarred them from My straight Path.

order.why: Set limited worldly days beside the call to awaken.
shortened: Say: O people! Fear ye God and the Manifestations of His Cause, and let not the world and its ornaments occupy you, for these shall pass away and are accounted before God as but numbered days. Raise your heads from the couches of heedlessness, then detach yourselves from all earthly things, and be not like those who forgot God and cast the words of God behind their backs, and were recorded in the Book of the righteous by the name of transgressors.

order.why: Hear the challenge to rise from heedlessness.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the worlds! How long will ye slumber upon the couch of heedlessness and desire? Lift up your heads - the Truth hath come with power and sovereignty.

order.why: Notice the difference between a raised call and an awakened listener.
shortened: The Day hath come, yet most of the people remain heedless. The Call hath been raised in truth, yet most of the people remain asleep.

order.why: Consider recognizing one’s station amid competing voices.
Read the command to take hold of the Book in its theological setting.
Connect opening one’s eyes with setting aside imagined certainties.
Consider the things that can hold a person back.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the earth! By God, the Most Great Book hath appeared and calleth all unto His luminous horizon. Beware lest the things of this world hold you back from the Lord of all being. Cast aside what ye possess and take what is with God, the Almighty, the Powerful.

order.why: Read the exchange of ornaments for commanded action.
Place relinquishment in the context of hope.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! Abandon that which ye possess, in hope of that which is with God. Thus doth He Who speaketh the truth command you.

order.why: Retain the short invitation to turn from possessions toward a horizon.
Read the strong statement about what will profit a listener.
shortened: O people of the earth! Abandon what ye possess, for He hath come with manifest sovereignty. Nothing shall profit you today save through His bidding, the Mighty, the Wondrous.

order.why: Identify relinquishment with removing whatever keeps one back.
Consider an illumined horizon that remains unrecognized.
shortened: O people! Turn ye unto the Supreme Horizon. By God! It hath been illumined by My Most Glorious Name, yet the people know not, save whom God willeth.

order.why: Turn with a radiant face from fancies toward the Hidden One.
shortened: Praise be to God Who hath spoken a Word whereby the fragrance of the Bayan was diffused and the ocean of certitude surged, and all things proclaimed: O peoples of earth and heaven! The Hidden One hath come with manifest sovereignty. Turn ye unto Him with radiant faces, and follow not the sources of idle fancies and vain imaginings.

order.why: Hear the All-Loving named within a demanding appeal.
shortened: Cast away what is with the people through the power of the Most Great Name and say: O people of the world, the Ancient Beauty hath come, and He Who was promised hath appeared and been recorded in the Tablets of God, the Lord of existence. Fear ye God and follow not your desires. Turn ye unto Him Who calleth you to the Most Exalted Station, from God, the Almighty, the All-Loving.

order.why: Invite a heart to hasten and a voice to speak praise.
shortened: Cast behind thee all mundane concerns, then speak forth in praise of thy Lord and say: O people! He Who was promised hath come unto you. Beware lest ye hesitate. Hasten unto Him with your hearts, for thus have ye been commanded in all the Tablets from God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Read longing as the motive for an urgent response.
shortened: When thou hast attained and drunk, say: O peoples of the earth! The veils have been rent asunder and the All-Bestowing hath come with manifest sovereignty. Say: This is not a day for tarrying; turn with your hearts, O ye heedless ones! The fire of longing hath been kindled in all regions - hasten, O ye lovers!

order.why: Answer a call described through merciful breezes and fulfillment.
Keep mercy and compassion central while circumstances press upon the listener.
shortened: Turn ye, O peoples of the earth, unto God, your Lord, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
Beware lest the conditions of creation withhold you from the remembrance of the Truth.

order.why: Preserve the injunction concerning obedience and association in its source setting.
shortened: O people! Hear My call and follow that which ye have been commanded in the Book of God. Then shun those who join partners with God.

order.why: Retain the strong command to follow the Speaker of truth.
Hear the invitation to turn on the Day of God.
Read the brief warning against wrongdoing.
shortened: Say: The Promised One hath come with the truth. Fear God, O people, and be not of the wrongdoers.

order.why: Keep the promised call from the Prisoner tied to moral response.
shortened: O thou who art mentioned before the Prisoner! The Promise hath come, and the Promised One proclaimeth with the most exalted call: "O concourse of earth and heaven! Fear ye the Lord of all mankind, and be not of the wrongdoers."

order.why: Return to the universal invitation toward God.
shortened: Say: O people of the earth! The Promise hath appeared and the Promised One hath come, calling all unto God, the Sovereign Lord of existence.

order.why: Let joy move a recipient toward assistance.
shortened: A Book sent down in truth to him who hath attained the light of God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting, that joy may seize him in such wise that he will arise to aid the Cause of his Lord and say: "O people! Follow Him Who hath come to you with manifest sovereignty."

order.why: Hear the short summons to arise and help.
shortened: Say: O people! The Day hath come. Arise to help your Lord, the Most Exalted, the Mighty, the All-Praised.

order.why: Read the urgent appeal for aid against the passing of possessions.
shortened: Say: O peoples of the earth! Fear God and follow not your idle fancies. Follow Him Who hath come unto you with a sovereignty before which all names have bowed down, and with a Cause against which no parties can prevail. Aid ye your Lord, the All-Merciful. Soon shall all that ye possess perish; then shall ye find yourselves in abasement and loss.

order.why: Preserve the blessing and warning with their original terms.
Name the moment as a Day of Covenant.
shortened: O peoples of the world! The Day of the Covenant has come, and He Who was hidden in the eternity of eternities has appeared.

order.why: Read all being called to that covenant.
shortened: He has appeared at the pole of the horizons and called all to the covenant, the station wherein the very atoms of its dust proclaim that there is no God but Me, the Most High, the Most Great.

order.why: End the unfolding images with the Herald’s announcement of an open heaven.
shortened: And the Herald has called out: "O people of earth! The gate of heaven has been opened and He Who was promised in the Books of God, the Lord of the seen and unseen, has come!"

order.why: Proclaims fulfillment of the promise and the opening of heaven’s gate.
Close by joining face, heart, ears, hands and feet in a response that becomes action.

questions: How do tranquility, dignity, and fair judgment affect the way a person receives a claim of religious renewal?
What does the contrast between imprisonment and proclaimed sovereignty invite you to consider about spiritual authority?
How do images of gates, water, light, and a speaking Book develop different aspects of the invitation?
What obstacles to hearing or recognition recur, and how might a reader examine them without assuming that disagreement proves another person’s bad faith?
How do the neighboring proclamations to particular religions and leaders help illuminate this worldwide address?
What might it mean for the promise of renewal to become visible in reform, the rejection of strife, and the actions of daily life?

references.label: 1 · Isaiah 55 · Hearing an invitation to life
references.note: Read the invitation to water without price, the call to listen and return, and the image of a divine word working like rain that makes the earth fruitful. Compare this with the compilation’s oceans, open gates, and appeals to the peoples of the world. How do these images join freely offered bounty with a response that changes life?
